headline: WESTGOLD PROFIT SURGES 452% IN FY26 — $480M NPAT on 387koz Record Output; $939M Treasury, $50M Buyback Approved
snippet: Westgold Resources (ASX/TSX: WGX) reported a record FY26 underlying NPAT of A$480 million — up 452% year-on-year — as gold revenue surged 79% to A$2,441 million on the back of record production of 387,354 ounces that beat the top end of its 345,000–385,000oz guidance range. The company remains 100% debt-free, fully unhedged, with a A$939 million treasury position (up A$575M for the full year), and the board declared a 10-cent fully franked final dividend worth roughly A$95 million. A A$50 million on-market buyback was approved for FY27, and Westgold has scheduled a full strategic outlook and FY27 guidance release for September 9, 2026. At $4,600+ gold, its Murchison and Southern Goldfields operations are generating free cash flow at a pace that puts most juniors' market caps to shame.

headline: COPPER SMASHES COMEX RECORD $6.73/lb — LME STOCKS FALL 42 STRAIGHT DAYS; HALF OF LONDON INVENTORY ALREADY EARMARKED OUT
snippet: Copper for September delivery surged to $6.7270 a pound ($14,830 a tonne) on the COMEX Friday, clearing the previous record set August 12, while LME warehouse stocks fell for a 42nd consecutive session — the longest uninterrupted decline since 2014 — to 204,975 tonnes, with nearly half already earmarked for withdrawal. The London cash premium over the three-month contract reached $207.50 a tonne, the widest backwardation of 2026, up from $34 at the end of July. The two-sided squeeze compounds already-severe supply disruption from the Kamoa-Kakula flooding and the DRC copper concentrate export ban. Junior copper explorers with advanced-stage resources in safe jurisdictions are the direct structural beneficiary of this market dislocation.

headline: JULY PCE HITS 3.7% YoY — Markets Now Price 38% CHANCE OF SEPTEMBER RATE HIKE; December Hike Odds Top 70%
snippet: The July U.S. PCE price index — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — rose 3.7% year-on-year, released Friday August 28, sustaining the overshoot that is complicating Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's approach after his hawkish Jackson Hole debut. Markets are now pricing a 38% probability of a September rate hike and above 70% odds of a December hike. Gold held near $4,594–$4,608 through the Friday session as the debasement trade absorbed dollar strength — reflecting the market view that the inflation-hike dynamic is net bullish for gold when US fiscal credibility is simultaneously under pressure. The correlation breakdown between rate hikes and gold selling is a structural shift worth tracking for resource-sector positioning.

headline: KORYX DRILLS 969m — LONGEST COPPER INTERSECTION EVER AT HAIB, NAMIBIA; Pre-Feasibility Study Due Year-End
snippet: Koryx Copper (TSX-V: KRY) released assay results from 19 drill holes totalling 8,586 metres at its wholly-owned Haib Copper Project in southern Namibia, anchored by HM167 returning 969 metres grading 0.27% copper equivalent from surface — the company's longest mineralised intersection ever at Haib. HM185 delivered 236 metres at 0.51% copper within a broader 413-metre envelope at 0.37% Cu, and HM177 hit 30 metres at 1.10% CuEq. All 19 holes intersected thick mineralisation above the current resource average grade, building support for a resource update and prefeasibility study targeted before year-end. Haib is one of the world's largest undeveloped copper deposits; consistent infill results beating the block model grade are exactly what copper-hungry majors need to see before making a move.

headline: LITHIUM IONIC CLOSES $37.5M SALINAS DEAL — PLS Pays $30M Cash at Close; Ionic Retains 2% Royalty on Future Spodumene
snippet: Lithium Ionic Corp. (TSX-V: LTH) completed the sale of its Salinas Group of lithium properties in Minas Gerais, Brazil — including the Baixa Grande lithium resource — to PLS Brasil Mineração, a wholly-owned subsidiary of PLS Group. PLS paid US$30 million cash at closing, with a further US$7.5 million deferred to the earlier of PLS's positive FID on the Colina Project or December 31, 2029. Lithium Ionic retained a 2.0% royalty on future spodumene sales from Baixa Grande, preserving upside exposure to the Brazil lithium district while monetising a non-core asset at lithium carbonate prices above $20,000/t — near double the year-ago level. Proceeds strengthen the balance sheet ahead of development decisions on Ionic's flagship Bandeira project.

headline: USA RARE EARTH CLOSES SERRA VERDE DEAL END OF AUGUST — $33.5M in US Government Grants Secured for Round Top
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) is completing its combination with Serra Verde — a Brazilian rare earth producer — by month-end, creating a vertically integrated heavy rare earth platform that spans mining, separation, and processing across two continents. The company has secured up to US$19.3 million from the DOE's Critical Minerals Innovation program and up to US$14.2 million from the Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund for its Round Top Heavy Rare Earth Project, adding $33.5 million in non-dilutive government capital. USAR reported Q2 revenue of US$6 million with $1.5 billion in cash; the Serra Verde acquisition brings operating mine output of separated neodymium-praseodymium and dysprosium. With China controlling roughly 85% of global rare earth refining, USAR's Western end-to-end supply model is attracting outsized policy and investment attention.

headline: CHINA SITS ON H2 RARE EARTH QUOTAS — September Key for Prices as Malaysia Eyes Easing Its Raw REE Export Ban
snippet: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has still not published its second-half 2026 mining and smelting quotas as of late August — identified by analysts as the single biggest near-term catalyst for rare earth prices heading into September. The delay stems from a February proposal to incorporate imported ore into the quota system, which faces opposition from companies dependent on overseas feedstock. Meanwhile, Malaysia is assessing whether to ease its 2024 moratorium on raw rare earth exports under pressure from investors in the US, Australia, France, and India seeking supply diversification. Erbium is the sole bright spot in an August rare earth price pullback, holding gains on fibre-optic and defence laser demand — a reminder of how narrowly specialised individual REE markets remain.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GDX BEST AUGUST ON RECORD — Gold Miners Up 43%, Retail Flooding In; New All-Time Highs by Year-End?
snippet: GoldSeek's analysis of the gold miner sector notes August 2026 is on track to be the strongest single month ever recorded for gold mining equities — GDX at $103.64, up 20.49% YTD with retail inflows of $419 million for the month. The piece asks whether the structural conditions — producers generating free cash flow at $4,500+ gold with AISCs that have risen far more slowly than the metal — can sustain a push to new all-time highs before December. The bear case is Kevin Warsh's rate path and a stronger dollar; the bull case is that senior producers are now returning more cash to shareholders than they can deploy organically, and the re-rating of the sector is forcing capital toward juniors with real resource stories. For retail investors who missed the senior rally, the thesis is now migrating down the market-cap ladder.

headline: NAI500: COPPER SMASHES RECORD — DRC Ban + Kamoa Outage + US Tariff Squeeze: Is $8/lb Next?
snippet: NAI 500's August analysis argues that copper's run above $6.70/lb may be a floor rather than a ceiling, identifying three simultaneous structural shocks: the DRC export ban on copper concentrate (cutting roughly 12% of global refined supply); the ongoing Kamoa-Kakula flooding and partial production curtailment; and US tariff-driven arbitrage systematically draining London and Shanghai exchange inventories. LME's 42-day inventory decline — the longest since 2014, with half the remaining stocks already earmarked for withdrawal — represents a near-term physical supply emergency. New mine supply requires 10–15 years to develop while EV and AI power-infrastructure demand curves are rising faster. The article models $8/lb as achievable in 2026 on supply shock alone, before structural demand from the energy transition fully materialises.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD AND SILVER STAGING POWERFUL BREAKOUTS — August Silver Surge 14% vs Gold 9%; Bull Market Entering Late Phase
snippet: GoldSeek's technical and fundamental read finds gold and silver both staging breakout patterns — gold holding above $4,580 support post-Warsh and silver recovering firmly past $70 despite dollar strength. Silver's 14% August gain versus gold's 9% is a historically reliable signal that the bull market is entering its later, more explosive phase when industrial demand amplifies investment demand. The silver-to-gold ratio compression strengthens the case for silver-focused junior miners with near-term production milestones. The piece cautions that Warsh's rate path introduces short-term volatility, but argues the debasement trade — driven by $2 trillion-plus US fiscal deficits — is structural regardless of near-term rate levels. A sustained move above $75 silver would close the gap to the all-time high and typically draws a new wave of generalist capital into the sector.
